answer: AI agents now search literature, generate hypotheses, plan experiments and in some cases order lab work. Cloud providers have entered: Amazon Bio Discovery combines biology foundation models with an agent interface and connected lab services in a closed loop.

reading.body:
AI agents in science work best on narrow, well specified steps, with a scientist approving each experiment the agent proposes.

The pattern in the data is a division of labor rather than autonomy. Agents search literature, generate hypotheses, and plan experiments, but the stated guidance keeps a human approving each proposed experiment. The one named platform, Amazon Bio Discovery, combines biology foundation models with an agent interface and connected lab services in a closed loop, which is the shape to watch: models plus an agent layer plus physical lab work.

That closed loop matters for AI because the agent is only one component. Foundation models supply the prediction, and connected lab services supply the execution. When the loop closes, the constraint shifts toward the physical side, the instruments and the wet lab that actually run the experiments.

The data does not say how many agents are deployed, how often they are correct, or what any of this costs. It covers one platform and one piece of operating advice, so it describes a direction rather than a measured trend.

explainer:
An AI agent takes a goal, breaks it into steps, uses tools such as search engines, databases and analysis software, and works through the steps with limited supervision. In science, agents are being built to read the literature and summarise what is known, propose hypotheses, design experiments, analyse results and, when connected to automated labs, order the experiments themselves.

The promise is to compress the cycle between idea and result. The current reality is narrower: agents work best on well defined steps such as literature synthesis, data analysis and experiment planning, and they can make confident mistakes that a scientist must catch. Cloud providers now offer agent platforms tied to biology models and lab services, which lowers the barrier for smaller teams. Good practice keeps a scientist approving any experiment an agent proposes and records the agent's reasoning for later review.

What an AI agent for science does

A science agent is given a research question rather than a single task. It searches the literature, proposes hypotheses, designs experiments or analyses, runs code against data, reads the results and revises its plan, using tools such as databases, simulation software and, where connected, automated laboratories. The idea is to compress the loop of reading, thinking and testing that a research group runs over months into something that runs continuously.

What has been demonstrated

Agents have reproduced published analyses from their methods sections, proposed candidate targets and compounds that were later confirmed in the lab, generated and tested hypotheses in computational biology, and written draft papers. Companies and academic groups have reported cases where an agent found an overlooked connection in the literature or a flaw in an analysis. The demonstrations are real, but they are selected; the proportion of agent proposals that lead anywhere is rarely reported.

How discovery teams are using them

The sober use is as a research assistant with unusual stamina: exhaustive literature synthesis, first pass analyses, systematic exploration of parameter spaces, and keeping track of everything tried. Scientists set the questions, judge the proposals and run or sanction the experiments. The governance questions are the same as for any agent, with one addition specific to science: an agent that can order experiments or reagents, or publish results, needs limits on exactly those actions, and its record keeping has to meet the standards of a laboratory notebook, because its work may one day support a patent or a filing.
